title: Upgrade GlusterFS on CentOS Stream 10 (stable)
summary: A step-by-step upgrade tutorial for CentOS Stream 10. Use the stable Eliware repository, verify package and service state at every checkpoint, and replace angle-bracket placeholders with values from your environment.

steps.title: Read the release notes
steps.text: Confirm the supported source-to-target path and read the target release warnings before changing a production cluster.
steps.verify: The target version and upgrade path are documented.

steps.title: Choose online or offline mode
steps.text: Online upgrades are for replicated or distributed-replicate volumes. Use offline mode for dispersed layouts. Do not change volume configuration during the upgrade; upgrade geo-replication slaves before the master and servers before clients.
steps.verify: The mode, maintenance window, and current heal state are recorded.

steps.title: Check removed options and deprecated features
steps.text: For older source releases, inspect the target-version warnings. In particular check features.lock-heal, features.grace-timeout, and deprecated translators listed by the target release.
steps.verify: Removed settings are unset or have an approved migration plan.

steps.title: Refresh the signed Eliware source
steps.text: Verify the stable candidate before stopping services.
steps.verify: The candidate comes from the intended signed channel.

steps.title: Upgrade one server
steps.text: For online mode, stop one server's Gluster services and GFAPI applications, update it, then start it before touching another server. Never take multiple members of one replica set down together.
commands: sudo systemctl stop glusterd glustereventsd 2>/dev/null || true
steps.verify: The upgraded server is healthy and all expected processes are online.

steps.title: Heal before continuing
steps.text: Invoke self-heal and wait for the backlog to clear or reach an approved steady state before upgrading the next server.
commands: for volume in $(gluster volume list); do gluster volume heal "$volume"; done
steps.verify: Peers are connected, volumes are online, and no unexpected backlog remains.

steps.title: Upgrade every remaining server and client
steps.text: Repeat the server sequence for every pool member. Then unmount client filesystems, stop GFAPI applications, update client packages, remount, and restart applications.
steps.verify: All servers and clients report the target version and mounts are healthy.

steps.title: Complete post-upgrade checks
steps.text: After the entire pool is upgraded, update op-version when appropriate, verify volume health, and document application tests. Follow the upstream reboot guidance for pre-7 clusters that ever used quota.
steps.verify: The cluster is healthy and the op-version decision is recorded.
